subject: Business
title: What Product-Market Fit Actually Means
description: One-minute skill: What Product-Market Fit Actually Means.

hook.text: Marc Andreessen says product-market fit is the only thing that matters for a startup.

buildup.text: It means making something a market is desperate to buy — not just willing to try.

discovery.text: When you have it, customers pull the product from your hands. Growth feels almost effortless.

twist.text: Before fit, everything feels like pushing a boulder uphill. After fit, you can barely keep up.

climax.text: Superhuman surveys users: 'How would you feel without us?' If 40% say devastated, that's fit.

punchline.text: If you have to convince people they need it, you don't have it.

quiz.question: What benchmark does Superhuman use for product-market fit?
options: 40% of users would be very disappointed without the product
Positive unit economics in quarter one

details.summary: Product-market fit is the moment when a product satisfies strong market demand so effectively that growth becomes organic, retention stays high, and customers become advocates. Marc Andreessen described it as being in a good market with a product that can satisfy that market's hunger.
details.whyItMatters: Product-market fit is the single most important milestone for any startup because nothing else matters without it. Marketing, hiring, and fundraising all become dramatically easier once genuine product-market fit is achieved.
takeaways: Product-market fit means the market pulls the product out of your hands through demand
Before fit, nothing works easily; after fit, everything accelerates dramatically
Marc Andreessen says it is the only thing that matters for a startup

faq.question: How do you know when you have achieved product-market fit?
faq.answer: Word of mouth drives significant organic growth. Usage grows faster than the team can support. Customers would be very disappointed if the product disappeared. Retention curves flatten rather than declining to zero. Sales cycles shorten. These are felt indicators, not single metrics.

faq.question: How long does it typically take to find product-market fit?
faq.answer: Two to three years is common for venture-backed startups. Some find it in months, others take longer. The key is measuring progress toward fit through customer feedback and retention data, not just hoping it will emerge. If fit has not improved after significant iteration, consider a pivot.
